title: Admin task-broker and shadow-playground for safe runbook testing
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight, sandboxed task-broker and "shadow-playground" that lets support engineers and platform owners run real runbook steps against a mirrored environment and simulated side-effects without touching production state. The broker will accept existing runbook steps as tasks, route to a safe executor (ephemeral namespace or simulator), capture detailed telemetry and diffs against a golden baseline, and surface regressions or risky side-effects before changes reach live runbooks. This is intended to reduce toil from manual dry-runs and to catch automation regressions earlier in the deployment flow.
acceptance_criteria: Can register an existing runbook step as a task and route it to the shadow executor
Shadow executor provides configurable isolation: noop-mode, dry-run-mode, and state-sim-mode
Captured telemetry includes input params, simulated outputs, timings, and a structured diff against expected effects
UI/CLI shows execution trace and suggested mitigation flags for risky actions
End-to-end flow demonstrated in a 2-hour runbook review session with Support and SRE teams
comments: 2025-02-11 - Spike complete: implemented PoC broker using isolated k8s namespaces + sidecar simulator. Observed ~120ms median overhead per synthetic task; acceptable for nightly dry-runs but we'll tune batching for manual sessions.
2025-02-14 - Decision: use existing runbook step schema (runlet format) rather than inventing new DSL to speed adoption. PM-approved.

2025-02-18 - Security review requested: storing simulated credentials in ephemeral vault entries. Raised ticket to SecOps for guidance; recommendation to use short-lived KMS keys. (See SecOps note in Confluence)
2025-02-22 - Design feedback (Sofia Martinez): add a visual diff showing changed resources and a severity score. Action: include severity heuristics and threshold config in telemetry payloads.
2025-02-28 - Eng review: opted for three isolation modes (noop,dry-run,state-sim). Trade-off: state-sim requires mock data loaders for certain services; added scope to estimate.
2025-03-01 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/221 implementing broker API + admission webhook for task validation. Needs two reviewer approvals.
2025-03-03 - QA note: flaky when parallelizing 50 concurrent tasks against simulator due to rate-limited test backend; mitigation: add concurrency knob and exponential backoff in worker pool.

2025-03-04 - Sprint sync: Scoped MVP for March release: core broker, noop and dry-run modes, telemetry capture, CLI for engineers. Remaining items (state-sim adapters, UI diff visualizer) moved to follow-up cycle.
review_feedback: PM (Riley Chen): MVP must ensure discoverability from Console; add a Console route to launch shadow runs from a runbook revision.
Design (Sofia Martinez): prefer color-graded severity tags and inline remediation suggestions rather than free-text alerts.
Security (Priya Kapoor): do not persist secrets from simulated runs; ephemeral handles only. Signed off conditionally once KMS integration is used.
SRE (Marcus Hale): log sampling is required to keep volume manageable; recommend 1:10 default sampling for nightly bulk-tests and full capture for manual runs.
mitigation_plan: If the simulator causes downstream failures, broker will automatically revert to noop-mode and notify on-call. A rollout can be limited to staging projects via a whitelist for first two weeks. Rate limits and backoff protect test backends.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Internal alpha - engineering and support teams only; feature flagged per-project
Week 2: Broader beta - add Console entry and invite PM/SRE to try; gather UX feedback
Week 3: Gradual enablement for staging runbooks; enable telemetry retention for 14 days
Week 4+: Optional enablement for low-risk production runbooks with dry-run-mode only
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on the broker and basic isolation modes. Follow-ups will cover adapters for specific services (datastores, queues), richer visual diff UX, and automated regression gating tied to CI for runbook changes. Consider measuring mean time to detect automation regressions after MVP.
next_steps: Get SecOps sign-off on ephemeral KMS flow (blocker)
Merge PR for broker API after 2 approvals
Add Console link and small onboarding guide for support users
Run a 2-hour tabletop with SRE and Support using three representative runbooks
